body:
# aggregator(comments): author and body caps split surrogate pairs — validateAuthor/validateNewComment raw-slice at 120/20,000, bypassing the #7694/#7711 capUnits guard

## Problem

`pm-stack/aggregator/src/comments.ts` caps dashboard-comment text with raw `slice`, none of it pair-safe:

- lines 96–98 — `validateAuthor`: `id.slice(0, 120)`, `label.slice(0, 120)`, `sessionId.slice(0, 120)`
- line 132 — `validateNewComment`: `body: b.body.trim().slice(0, 20_000)`

This is the #3178 defect class that #7694 fixed for `actions.ts` `cleanText` and #7711 fixed for `markResult` via the `capUnits` helper (actions.ts:292, module-private): an astral character straddling the cap is dropped whole. The comments boundary was not audited in either fix — and it matters more here, because `validateAuthor` is the SHARED author validator: `actions.ts` (lines 154, 329) and `roadmap-annotations.ts` (lines 55, 80) both import it from `comments.ts`, so the pair-safe actions store still persists split-pair author ids/labels through this door, and roadmap annotations inherit the same defect.

The values are persisted, not just displayed: comments are written to the comments JSON store (`CommentsStore.persist`, comments.ts:259–264, `JSON.stringify` + atomic rename), so a split pair is stored as a lone `\ud83d` and any UTF-8 round-trip (file read, HTTP response) replaces it with U+FFFD.

Note on fix shape: `capUnits` cannot simply be imported from `actions.ts` — `actions.ts` imports `validateAuthor` from `comments.ts`, so that direction would create a module cycle. A local helper in `comments.ts` (or a shared helper in `validate.ts`, which `comments.ts` already imports) avoids the cycle.

## Evidence (verified this run, laptop primary @ f9dfb4cfa5, real module md5 567b6272246f4fcf519fe3213b490389)

Probe `~/git/fleet/probe-comments-surrogate/probe.ts` (bun, imports the real `comments.ts`):

```
label straddle | len: 120   | lone high surrogate at end: true  | utf8 roundtrip changes: true
label control   | len: 120   | lone: false | roundtrip changes: false
id straddle     | len: 120   | lone: true  | roundtrip changes: true
body straddle   | ok: true   | len: 20000 | lone: true  | roundtrip changes: true
body control    | ok: true   | len: 20000 | lone: false | roundtrip changes: false
json stored label last unit: d83d
```

- Straddle cases: label/id = 119 × `x` + 😀 + tail → capped value is 120 units ending in lone `\ud83d`; comment body = 19,999 × `z` + 😀 + tail → 20,000 units ending in lone `\ud83d`.
- Controls: pair fully inside the cap (118 × `x` + 😀; 19,998 × `z` + 😀) → value intact, round-trips cleanly.
- The JSON persistence round-trip preserves the lone surrogate as `\ud83d` in the stored record.

Dedup: searches for "validateAuthor surrogate", "comments surrogate", "DashAuthor slice", and "surrogate" (open + closed) return no issue for these caps; #7694/#7711 cover `actions.ts` text fields only, #7725 covers `activity.ts` summary caps — neither touches the shared author validator or the comment body cap.

## Why it matters

- Author labels and comment bodies are operator/user text — an emoji at the wrong offset permanently corrupts the stored author identity or comment body (U+FFFD in the persisted store, and in every action/annotation record that carries the same author).
- Because `validateAuthor` is shared, this is the residual door for the two fixes that landed this morning: #7694/#7711 made action text pair-safe while the author on those same records can still be split.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All four caps in `comments.ts` (author id/label/sessionId at 120, comment body at 20,000) are surrogate-pair-safe: an astral character straddling the cap is dropped whole, never split (mirroring `capUnits` semantics from #7711), without introducing a module import cycle.
- [ ] Regression tests in the aggregator suite pin the straddle case for the author label (or id) cap and the comment body cap, plus an exact-fit control (pair fully inside the cap stays intact); the new tests fail on the pre-fix code.
- [ ] The existing aggregator test suite stays green.
